chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Saweed, from Al-Daras ibn Abi Mansoor, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
Three things that people cannot endure: Forbearing with people, a brother supporting his brother in his wealth, and remembering God often.
ai.seo_question: What are the three difficult virtues mentioned by Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifying three virtues that transcend human nature: forgiving others, sharing wealth with one's brother, and frequent remembrance of God (dhikr). These acts are considered difficult because they require overcoming the ego's desire for retribution, greed, and heedlessness, thereby elevating the believer to a state of spiritual excellence (ihsan).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-142 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Nazr ibn Soweed, on the authority of Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Ya’fur that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
There are three things that are really hard for the people: forgiving the faults of others; accepting that others have more wealth than they do; and remembering God often.”
